title: Can you poll artists: Bach and Beethoven
summary: Ridley argues that comparing individual artists in polls makes no sense.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Well let me ask you this, to interject something along the lines. You're talking about those polls. One of the questions I asked you at the very beginning about jazz being an art form kind of music as opposed to the commercial kind of thing. The thing that has always bothered me about this poll business, I mean you're talking about a person, okay, you're an individual, I'm an individual. All the people you've named are individuals. I mean it seems to me when you start talking about an art form and artists, I mean, how do you use a commercial kind of poll to do that kind of thing because we're talking about individuals and individual creativity and expressions of their creativity. How are you ever going to conduct a poll? I don't ever see them comparing Bach and Beethoven. You know each is accepted for what the individual does as an individual artist-composer, you know or Rembrandt and Picasso. I don't hear nobody comparing, you don't have no poll saying which is greater than the other. You know and how can you compare and say that Lester Young is greater than
Coleman Hawkins or vice versa. You know, that's what bothers me personally about the polls.
